category_title: Reserved students who limit participation to interactions with adults
student_description: Amber is a reserved student who struggles to engage in unstructured group activities and rarely volunteers ideas spontaneously. She uniquely requires direct, one-on-one adult attention, specific targeted questions, and strong positive social reinforcement to participate and build confidence. Over time, she needs carefully designed scaffolding to help her transition from relying on adult prompts to formulating her own questions and goals.

criteria.rationale: To move beyond relying solely on adult attention, Amber needs structured environments that gradually build her capacity to ask her own questions and self-regulate.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes specific task designs or strategies aimed at transitioning Amber from answering direct adult questions to formulating her own questions and goals.

criteria.rationale: Since Amber currently avoids unstructured group interaction, carefully designed scaffolding from others is necessary to support her long-term interest development.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates structured support or 'scaffolding from others' (peers or mentors) in a deliberate way that builds her interest without relying on unstructured group work.
